::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Easter Eve [4 April 1896]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Charlotte Mitchell
:::

My dear [Mrs Selwyn](people/person_1297.qmd)
I have been begged to find out whence came a beautiful prayer that was given to all your friends at your first start to N Z.  It really seems like going into the last century, or the primitive Church, and I do not suppose there is anybody who could tell me now, not even [Fanny Patteson](people/person_1151.qmd), so I am venturing to ask whether you can remember.  The new [Bishop of Osaka](people/person_85.qmd) (Japan) has had it printed on his farewell cards sent to all his friends.  He was to land either last Monday or on Good Friday at Nagasaki, a considerable difference in speed since your time![^1]

I hope you are well.  This warm winter has been very kind to many and we have hosts of primroses for the decorations to which I am just going

yours affectionately
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: In fact it was reported in *The Times* (30 May 1896) that the Awdrys did not reach Japan until 27 April.  When Mrs Selwyn first went to New Zealand in 1842 she travelled by sailing ship round the Cape;  by the 1890s the Suez Canal (1869) and the steamship had shortened the journey by several months.
